name: Vegetable potjie
summary: Butternut, baby potatoes, mielies, peppers and chickpeas layered in a three-legged pot and slow-simmered over coals in a smoky tomato sauce.
about: Potjiekos, 'little-pot food', is cooked outdoors in a round cast-iron potjie over a slow fire, with the ingredients layered and left unstirred so each keeps its shape. It grew from the pioneer habit of keeping a pot going on the fire. A vegetable potjie lets everyone at a meat braai share the pot, and it is happily eaten with potbrood, rice or pap.

ingredients.name: Butternut
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into 4 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Mielies
ingredients.note: corn on the cob, each cut into 3

ingredients.name: Vegetable stock
ingredients.note: made with a stock cube or powder

ingredients.name: Sweet peppers
ingredients.note: red and yellow, cut into strips

steps: Make a fire and let it burn down to medium coals: you should be able to hold your hand at grid height for about 6 seconds. Set a No. 3 potjie on its legs over a small heap of coals and let it heat for 5 minutes.
Add the oil and onions and fry, stirring, until soft and golden, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, paprika, cumin and thyme for 1 minute until fragrant, then the tomato paste for another minute.
Layer the hardest vegetables over the onions without stirring: first the carrots, then the potatoes, then the butternut and the mielie pieces.
Mix the tomatoes, stock, sugar, salt and pepper and pour it over the vegetables. Tuck in the bay leaves, put on the lid and bring to a gentle bubble.

Pull most of the coals away so that only a few sit under the pot, enough to keep a lazy simmer. Cook covered for 50 minutes without stirring, adding a few fresh coals every 20 minutes and a splash of water if the bottom sounds dry rather than bubbling.

Scatter the chickpeas, peppers, baby marrows and green beans on top, replace the lid and simmer for another 25 minutes, until a knife slides easily through the potatoes and butternut and the beans are bright and just tender.

Take the pot off the coals, gently fold the layers together once, taste for salt and scatter with parsley. Serve straight from the pot with potbrood, rice or pap. (On a stove: use a heavy casserole over low heat with the same timings.)
prepNote: Peel and cut the vegetables a few hours ahead and keep them in the fridge in separate bags.
